title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
statement: You are given `prices`, where `prices[i]` is the price of a stock on day i. Choose one day to buy and a later day to sell. Return the maximum profit. If no profit is possible, return 0.
hints: Every pair of days is a candidate, but only later days can be sell days.
The best sell on day i is prices[i] minus the cheapest price seen before i.
Track the minimum price so far and the best difference in one left-to-right pass.

approaches.name: All pairs
approaches.explanation: Try every buy day and every later sell day.

approaches.name: Running minimum
approaches.explanation: Sell against the lowest price observed so far.

editorial: A profitable sale on day i must buy at the minimum of prices[0..i-1]. Maintain that minimum while scanning, and keep the largest nonnegative difference. One pass is enough because every earlier price has already competed for the minimum.
reference_solution:
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
from collections import Counter, OrderedDict, defaultdict, deque
import heapq

def max_profit(prices: list[int]) -> int:
    best = 0
    low = prices[0]
    for price in prices[1:]:
        best = max(best, price - low)
        low = min(low, price)
    return best

examples.explanation: Prices only fall, so the profit is 0.
